description: How I designed this site so that the numbers shown are recalculated instead of copied.
texte: The problem A proof page written by hand always ends up lying. You write “18 tests”, then add three more, and the page still says 18. Nobody notices, except a buyer who counts. The answer Each project has a manifest, store/projets/<slug>/preuve.yml , which says where its evidence comes from: the test file, the command to run, the SQL query, the files to measure. When the site is built, the engine runs those commands and injects the result. The consequence: if I delete a test, the number drops. If a delivered file disappears, the build fails. description: A single global proof page proves nothing to anyone. Here is what I did instead.
texte: A week ago, this site had one proof page. It said: “35 tests, the MQTT chain works, the addresses are read back”. That is true, and it is useless. The problem A visitor buying the greenhouse kit does not care about the self-monitoring layer’s tests. A client who wants a self-hosting guide does not care about the humidity sensor’s CRC. Putting all three on one page asks the reader to sort them out — and an argument that needs sorting is not an argument. The answer Each project now has its own proof page, right where it is sold.
